proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1 and a real number t with (n-1)/n <= t < 1. Let k be any integer with 1 <= k <= n.

From t >= (n-1)/n, multiplying by the positive integer k gives
kt >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.
Because k <= n, we have k/n <= 1, so k - k/n >= k - 1. Hence kt >= k - 1.

Also, since t < 1 and k > 0, multiplying by k yields kt < k.

Therefore k - 1 <= kt < k. Since k - 1 is an integer, the definition of the floor function implies
floor(kt) = k - 1.

This holds for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n, as required.
solver_summary: Use the bounds (n-1)/n <= t < 1 to show k-1 <= kt < k for each 1 <= k <= n; then the floor is k-1.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly establishes that for any integer k with 1 <= k <= n and any t in [(n-1)/n, 1), one has k-1 <= kt < k, hence floor(k*t)=k-1. The quantifiers match the lemma statement and there is no semantic drift.
